**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a soybean leaf (upper surface) with:
- 2-3 large, irregular dark brown lesions (~1-2 cm)
- Prominent **yellow-green halos** surrounding each lesion
- **Dead tissue falling out** leaving distinct holes (ragged appearance)
- Green leaf background; background plants showing some yellowing

**Matching against candidates:**

| Disease | Match |
|---|---|
| Bacterial_Blight | ✅ "yellowish-green halos"; "dead tissue falls out giving ragged appearance"; angular to irregular lesions |
| Phyllosticta_leaf_spot | Partial — reference showed yellow halos, but description says "purplish margins"; lesions described as lower canopy, cool conditions |
| Frogeye_leaf_spot | Partial — gray centers with reddish-brown borders, not yellow halos |
| Septoria_brown_spot | ❌ Very small scattered dark dots, not large lesions with halos |
| Cercospora | ❌ Purple-bronze blighting of entire leaf surface |
| Downy_mildew | ❌ Pale yellow spots + gray tufts on underside |
| Soybean_rust | ❌ Tiny tan pustules |

The **yellow-green halos** combined with **tissue dropout creating holes** is the most distinctive match for Bacterial_Blight. The lesions are larger/rounder than typical early-stage bacterial blight but can enlarge and coalesce. Phyllosticta is described as having purplish (not yellow) margins, making it less consistent.
